transcript.text: Hi, our integrated fridge freezer (behind a kitchen door) - the fridge is around 10 degrees but the freezer seems ok. We had a power cut a week ago, not sure if related. Rented flat, can't really take it out.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. A fridge at about 10°C is too warm for chilled food. With the freezer apparently still working, the most likely issue is that cold air is not reaching the fridge properly — commonly an ice build-up in the freezer air channels — rather than the whole cooling system having failed. The power cut could also have reset a temperature or holiday/eco setting. 1. Check the controls: set the fridge to about 3–5°C and freezer to –18°C. Make sure holiday, eco or demo mode is not selected. If a setting was wrong, allow 24 hours with the doors mostly shut to recover. 2. Check inside both compartments: make sure food is not pressed against any vents, especially at the back/top of the fridge. Also check the fridge door closes flat and the rubber seal is not folded, dirty or gapped. A blocked vent or poor seal can leave the fridge warm. 3. Look at the back wall inside the freezer without dismantling anything. A thick frost layer or solid-looking sheet of ice points to a defrost/airflow fault; the freezer can remain cold while the fridge warms up. Do not worry about pulling the integrated appliance out at this stage. If the settings and vents are fine but there is heavy ice, report it to the landlord/agent: it may need a full defrost and, if it returns, an engineer to diagnose the defrost system or freezer fan.
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

Thanks! There's no display, just a dial inside, and it's on 3 out of 5. My thermometers say fridge 10C and freezer -16C. There's some frost on the back wall of the freezer but not loads. The fridge door closes ok, though the cabinet door moves with it, and I can't see any vents in the fridge. No burning smell and nothing's tripped, by the way.

Also, the freezer is at –16°C rather than the usual target of about –18°C, so this may be reduced cooling overall rather than a fridge-only airflow problem. 1. Turn the dial to 5 (the coldest setting). Keep the doors closed as much as practical and recheck both thermometers after 24 hours. Put the fridge thermometer in the middle of the compartment, not against the back wall or in the door. - If the fridge comes down to 3–5°C and the freezer reaches roughly –18°C, the dial setting was simply too mild for the current conditions.
• If the freezer improves but the fridge remains near 10°C, restricted air circulation or an ice build-up becomes more likely.
• If neither improves, report it to the landlord/agent. A thermostat/control fault or a cooling-system fault then needs an engineer; the latter is not a DIY repair, especially on an integrated appliance. For now, avoid keeping high-risk chilled foods at 10°C (for example cooked leftovers, meat, fish and dairy) unless they can be moved to a reliably cold fridge or used promptly.
Ok, I'll turn it up to 5 and check the thermometers again tomorrow. Is there anything else I should do in the meantime?

Yes. In the meantime, keep the doors shut as much as you can and avoid overfilling the fridge or packing food tightly against the back wall; that gives the cold air the best chance to circulate. Keep high-risk chilled food somewhere reliably below 5°C if possible, rather than relying on a fridge reading 10°C. Also check the fridge door seal closely all the way round. A door can appear to close normally but still admit warm room air if the rubber is dirty, folded, split or coming away. With the appliance switched off and unplugged, wipe any dirt off with warm soapy water and make sure the seal sits flat. If it is visibly damaged or detached, report that to the landlord/agent. If, after 24 hours at setting 5, the freezer is near –18°C but the fridge remains around 10°C, restricted airflow becomes more likely. If both compartments remain too warm, a thermostat/control fault or a sealed cooling-system fault is more likely and the landlord should arrange an engineer.

claimsRejected.claim: The fridge is not back below 5°C.

candidates: Restricted cold-air flow from freezer to fridge, often from ice build-up in a frost-free system (high)
Temperature setting or holiday/eco mode changed after the power cut (medium)
Blocked internal vents or a door that is not sealing (medium)

plan: The fault they reported is: "fridge is around 10°C while freezer seems okay". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
